advances: The original-source curvature absorption and averaged transverse-noise estimates give a uniform cap at the full mean for every finite independent product of the original three-height laws with nonnegative common transverse tilts. The cap is independent of all row dimensions, row counts, budgets, tilts, and projection directions. This is a theorem for this source class, not a final result for the locked mixed-integer-volume problem.
author: research-agent
proof:
We first work in one row and suppress its index. Thus \(m=m_i\), \(h=h_i\), \(L=L_i\), \(\beta=\beta_i\), \(\theta=\theta_i\), \(j=j_i\), \(\mathbf a=\mathbf a^{(i)}\), and \(t=t_i\). Write \(X_\Sigma:=\sum_{k=1}^mX_k\), \(B_y:=L-hy\), \(\mu_y:=\mathbb E[X_\Sigma\mid Y=y]\), and \(v_y:=\operatorname{Var}(X_\Sigma\mid Y=y)\). These are exactly the conditional total means and variances in 43cb56218b18ec82; its \(v_1\) is our middle-slice \(v_1\). Put \(p_y:=\Pr(Y=y)\).

The original support contains a positive-probability point with \(X_1>0\), so its integer coordinate mean satisfies \(j\ge1\). The original slack \(L-X_\Sigma-hY\) is nonnegative and is strictly positive at the positive-probability origin. Its mean is the integer \(L-mj-h\), so \(L-mj-h\ge1\). In particular \((j\mathbf1_m,1)\) belongs to the original support, and \(B_1\ge m+1\). The height support is exactly \(\{0,1,2\}\). Since \(\mathbb EY=1\), its original endpoint probabilities satisfy \(p_0=p_2\). Denote their common value by \(\varepsilon\), so \(p_1=1-2\varepsilon\).

For completeness, we verify \(p_1\ge1/3\) directly for all \(\beta\ge0\), including zero. Use the same original transverse partition function as 43cb56218b18ec82,
\[
 Z_m(B,u):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf x\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^m\\\sum_kx_k\le B}}
                    e^{u\sum_kx_k}
          =\sum_{s=0}^B\binom{s+m-1}{m-1}e^{us}.
\]
The counting identity follows by placing \(m-1\) separators among \(s\) units. For a fixed real \(u\), set \(w_s:=\binom{s+m-1}{m-1}e^{us}\). The ratios \(w_{s+1}/w_s=e^u(s+m)/(s+1)\) are nonincreasing. Consequently, for \(B\ge1\) and \(1\le s\le B\), \(w_{B+1}w_{s-1}\le w_Bw_s\). Summing gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 w_{B+1}Z_m(B-1,u)&\le w_B\sum_{s=1}^B w_s<w_BZ_m(B,u),\\
 Z_m(B,u)^2-Z_m(B-1,u)Z_m(B+1,u)
 &=w_BZ_m(B,u)-w_{B+1}Z_m(B-1,u)>0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus successive differences of \(\log Z_m(B,u)\) decrease. Summing them over the two consecutive budget intervals of length \(h\), including an interval starting at budget zero when \(B_2=0\), yields \(Z_m(B_0,\beta)Z_m(B_2,\beta)\le Z_m(B_1,\beta)^2\).

The original probabilities are proportional to \(Z_m(B_0,\beta)\), \(e^\theta Z_m(B_1,\beta)\), and \(e^{2\theta}Z_m(B_2,\beta)\). Their equal endpoints give \(e^{2\theta}Z_m(B_2,\beta)=Z_m(B_0,\beta)\). Hence the probabilities remain exactly
\[
 \varepsilon=\frac{\sqrt{Z_m(B_0,\beta)Z_m(B_2,\beta)}}
 {Z_m(B_1,\beta)+2\sqrt{Z_m(B_0,\beta)Z_m(B_2,\beta)}},
 \qquad p_1=1-2\varepsilon\ge\frac13.
\]
In particular the involution \(y\mapsto2-y\) preserves the original height law.

Set \(\bar a:=m^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^m a_k\), \(Y^\circ:=Y-1\), and \(\Omega:=\mu_0+\mu_2-2\mu_1\). Here \(\Omega\) has precisely the original-source meaning in 43cb56218b18ec82. By permutation symmetry, \(\mathbb E[\mathbf X\mid Y=y]=(\mu_y/m)\mathbf1_m\). The values at the three heights give the exact interpolation identity
\[
 \mu_Y=\mu_1+\frac{\mu_2-\mu_0}{2}Y^\circ+\frac{\Omega}{2}(Y^\circ)^2,
 \qquad
 mj=\mathbb E\mu_Y=\mu_1+\varepsilon\Omega.
\]
Define the scalar variables
\[
\begin{aligned}
 W&:=\left(t+\bar a\frac{\mu_2-\mu_0}{2}\right)Y^\circ,\\
 V&:=\frac{\bar a\Omega}{2}((Y^\circ)^2-2\varepsilon),\\
 N&:=\mathbf a\cdot(\mathbf X-\mathbb E[\mathbf X\mid Y]),
 \qquad \sigma^2:=\mathbb EN^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
These are the scalar \(W,V,N\) and noise variance of b0f9a49859be646c, with its latent element equal to the original \(Y\). They have the pointwise identity
\[
 \mathbf a\cdot(\mathbf X-j\mathbf1_m)+t(Y-1)=W+V+N.
\]
Indeed the conditional mean of the left side is \(\bar a(\mu_Y-mj)+tY^\circ\), and the displayed interpolation yields \(W+V\). Under \(y\mapsto2-y\), \(Y^\circ\) changes sign and \((Y^\circ)^2\) stays fixed, so \(W\) is odd and \(V\) is even. Also \(\mathbb EV=0\) because \(\mathbb E(Y^\circ)^2=2\varepsilon\), and \(\mathbb E[N\mid Y]=0\) by its definition. All these equalities concern the original experiment.

The accepted theorem 9ba4a3963a51edd3 applies to precisely this \(N\) and these original parameters, and gives
\(\mathbb EN^4\le3\cdot10^{11}\sigma^4\).
We next control \(V\) by the same noise variance. Put \(\mathbf a^\perp:=\mathbf a-\bar a\mathbf1_m\), so \(\sum_k a_k^\perp=0\). Given \((Y,X_\Sigma)=(y,s)\), permutation symmetry gives \(\mathbb E[X_k\mid Y=y,X_\Sigma=s]=s/m\). Thus \(\mathbb E[\mathbf a^\perp\cdot\mathbf X\mid Y,X_\Sigma]=0\), including \(m=1\), where \(\mathbf a^\perp=\mathbf0\). Since
\(N=\bar a(X_\Sigma-\mu_Y)+\mathbf a^\perp\cdot\mathbf X\), the mixed second moment vanishes, and
\[
 \sigma^2=\bar a^2\sum_{y=0}^2p_yv_y+\mathbb E(\mathbf a^\perp\cdot\mathbf X)^2
          \ge\bar a^2p_1v_1\ge\frac{\bar a^2v_1}{3}.
\]
No comparison with a replacement conditional distribution is used here.

Suppose first that \(\beta>0\). All hypotheses of 43cb56218b18ec82 hold: the original parameters are finite, \(\beta\ne0\), and the full mean is the specified integer mean with \(j\ge1\). Therefore \(\varepsilon\Omega^4\le2^{36}v_1^2\). The variable \((Y^\circ)^2\) is Bernoulli with its original parameter \(q:=2\varepsilon\). Its centered fourth moment satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E((Y^\circ)^2-q)^4
 =q(1-q)^4+(1-q)q^4
 =q(1-q)((1-q)^3+q^3)\le q,
\]
because \(0\le q\le1\) and \((1-q)^3+q^3\le1\). Consequently
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb EV^4
 &\le\frac{\bar a^4\Omega^4}{16}\,2\varepsilon
  \le2^{33}\bar a^4v_1^2\\
 &\le9\cdot2^{33}\sigma^4
  \le3\cdot10^{11}\sigma^4.
\end{aligned}
\]
The final comparison holds because \(9\cdot2^{33}=77309411328<300000000000\). These inequalities do not divide by \(\bar a\) or \(\sigma\), so they include zero coefficients and zero noise variance.

If \(\beta=0\), we do not apply 43cb56218b18ec82. Instead the original conditional law at budget \(B_y\) is uniform on \(\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^m:\sum_kx_k\le B_y\}\). Appending the slack \(B_y-\sum_kx_k\) bijects it with the uniform complete compositions of \(B_y\) into \(m+1\) coordinates. Permutation symmetry of those \(m+1\) coordinates makes each coordinate's mean \(B_y/(m+1)\), so \(\mu_y=m(L-hy)/(m+1)\). This is affine in \(y\), including budget zero. Hence \(\Omega=0\) and \(V=0\), giving the same fourth-moment bound directly. The averaged-noise bound from 9ba4a3963a51edd3 already includes \(\beta=0\).

Restore the row indices to the exact definitions above, obtaining \(W_i,V_i,N_i\) and \(\sigma_i^2=\mathbb EN_i^2\). The full experiments \((Y_i,N_i)\) are independent because they are measurable functions of the independent original rows. For every row, its original latent involution is \(y\mapsto2-y\); it preserves the original endpoint probabilities and makes \(W_i\) odd and \(V_i\) even. We have proved \(\mathbb EV_i=0\), \(\mathbb E[N_i\mid Y_i]=0\), and
\[
 \mathbb EN_i^4\le K\sigma_i^4,
 \qquad \mathbb EV_i^4\le K\sigma_i^4,
 \qquad K:=3\cdot10^{11}\ge1.
\]
The sum \(T\) in the statement is pointwise \(\sum_i(W_i+V_i+N_i)\). Apply the independent-row sum extension of b0f9a49859be646c once, with this \(K\) and these exact original experiments. It gives both claimed cap probabilities at least \(1/(196608K)=c_+\), and gives the stronger \(1/2\) bound when \(\sum_i\sigma_i^2=0\). This application imposes no bound on the number of rows or their dimensions and no moment restriction on their odd terms.

Finally, the original mean belongs to each row support by the slack calculation, hence \(\bar{\mathbf z}\) belongs to their product. A closed halfspace containing \(\bar{\mathbf z}\) can be written as \(\{\mathbf z:\ell\cdot\mathbf z\ge u\}\), where \(u\le\ell\cdot\bar{\mathbf z}\). It contains \(\{\mathbf z:\ell\cdot(\mathbf z-\bar{\mathbf z})\ge0\}\). Splitting \(\ell\) into its original row coefficients makes the latter event exactly \(\{T\ge0\}\), whose original product probability is at least \(c_+\). A zero direction gives probability one directly. Throughout the proof the source probabilities, full-vector mean, and conditional laws remain those originally specified.
statement:
Let \(b\ge1\) be an integer. For each \(1\le i\le b\), let \(m_i,h_i,L_i\ge1\) be integers with \(2h_i\le L_i<3h_i\), let \(\beta_i\ge0\) and \(\theta_i\in\mathbb R\) be finite, and let \((\mathbf X^{(i)},Y_i)\) have the strictly positive original law
\[
 R_i(\mathbf x,y)=\frac{\exp(\beta_i\sum_{k=1}^{m_i}x_k+\theta_i y)}{\mathcal Z_i},
 \qquad
 (\mathbf x,y)\in E_{L_i,h_i,m_i}
 :=\left\{(\mathbf x,y)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{m_i+1}:
          \sum_{k=1}^{m_i}x_k+h_i y\le L_i\right\},
\]
where \(\mathcal Z_i\) is the original normalizing constant. Suppose the full mean in row \(i\) is \(\mathbb E(\mathbf X^{(i)},Y_i)=(j_i\mathbf1_{m_i},1)\), with integer \(j_i\), and suppose the full row experiments are independent.

For arbitrary \(\mathbf a^{(i)}\in\mathbb R^{m_i}\) and \(t_i\in\mathbb R\), define the original centered projection
\[
 T:=\sum_{i=1}^b\left[
       \mathbf a^{(i)}\cdot(\mathbf X^{(i)}-j_i\mathbf1_{m_i})
       +t_i(Y_i-1)\right].
\]
Then, with the single absolute constant \(c_+:=1/(196608\cdot3\cdot10^{11})\),
\[
 \min\{\Pr(T\ge0),\Pr(T\le0)\}\ge c_+.
\]
The full mean \(\bar{\mathbf z}:=((j_i\mathbf1_{m_i},1))_{i=1}^b\) belongs to the product of the original lattice supports. Every closed halfspace containing \(\bar{\mathbf z}\) therefore has probability at least \(c_+\) under the original product law. All statements include \(m_i=1\), \(L_i-2h_i=0\), \(\beta_i=0\), and zero projection directions. Write \(N_i:=\mathbf a^{(i)}\cdot(\mathbf X^{(i)}-\mathbb E[\mathbf X^{(i)}\mid Y_i])\) for the original conditional transverse noise and \(\sigma_i^2:=\mathbb EN_i^2\). If \(\sum_i\sigma_i^2=0\), both projection probabilities are at least \(1/2\).

The accepted predecessors used are the original-source absorption theorem 43cb56218b18ec82, the nonnegative-tilt averaged-noise theorem 9ba4a3963a51edd3, and the independent-row odd-center/even-drift/noise sum cap b0f9a49859be646c. The scalar variables used to apply the last lemma are defined explicitly in the proof; its latent variables are exactly the original heights, without any change of law or probabilities.
